site.title: Niko Kids Clinic
site.tagline: A paediatric clinic in Minato-Kita for babies, children and teenagers: same-day appointments, vaccinations and calm check-ups.

categories.name: Vaccines
categories.description: Schedules, flu season and what to expect.

posts.title: A fever at night: when to wait and when to call
posts.excerpt: Most fevers can wait until morning. Here are the signs that cannot.
posts.content:
A high temperature at two in the morning is frightening, but the number itself tells us less than how your child looks. A child who drinks, wakes easily and plays a little when the fever drops can usually wait until our morning slots open.

Call the children’s helpline or go to the emergency room if your baby is under three months, if your child is hard to wake, breathes fast or with effort, has a rash that does not fade when pressed, or stops drinking. When in doubt, call: that is what the line is for.

posts.title: Flu vaccines for this autumn
posts.excerpt: Who needs two doses, when to book and how we make the shot easier.
posts.content:
Flu vaccine slots for children aged six months to fifteen years are now open. Children under thirteen who have never had a flu vaccine need two doses about four weeks apart, so book the first one before the end of October.

Bring the health handbook to every visit. We offer numbing patches for nervous children, and you can book siblings back to back so the family only waits once.

posts.title: Sleep and screens: small changes that help
posts.excerpt: Three habits our families say made bedtime easier.
posts.content:
Many parents ask us about sleep at check-ups. The advice that helps most is also the simplest: the same bedtime every night, a dark and cool room, and no screens for an hour before bed.

Start with one change, not three. Keep a short diary for two weeks and bring it to your next visit; we will look at it together and adjust the plan for your child’s age.
